articles.title: A faster algorithm for extracting hexadecimal digits of π
articles.summary: The new algorithm for extracting hexadecimal digits of π without computing the preceding digits beats the standard term-by-term evaluations of Bailey–Borwein–Plouffe (BBP), Bellard, and Huvent on operation count. It saves about 61% fewer divisions and 38% fewer full modular exponentiations compared to Huvent's eight-term formula. The algorithm relies on a relationship among the four powers of two in the identity for π, and it uses a common denominator to add four remainders and divide once, eliminating the need to compute those remainders independently.

articles.title: From formal verification to bug-finding in CHERIoT
articles.summary: Cerise, a project started at Aarhus University 10 years ago, aims to develop formal methods for verifying properties of capability machines, particularly non-monotonicity, and proving end-to-end results in the presence of unknown code. The project has been extended to model different aspects of capability machines and has collaborated with other universities. Cerise's approach has evolved over time, scaling up from foundational proofs to reason about a wider range of properties, including MMIO and attestation, and working with an instruction set closer to the CHERIoT Sail model. The project's findings, including two bugs in the CHERIoT switcher, highlight the importance of reasoning about unknown code, which is challenging due to the need to account for indirect interactions with unknown compartments.
